data.content_ref: inline:The target justifies the §11.3 flag by asserting the ritual is an information-theoretic bottleneck that inevitably forces a loss of soundness or relevance for any high-dimensional claim. But the adjudication-ritual standard (§11.3) governs whether sustained flags were correctly upheld; the target concedes the flag is 'sustained' yet simultaneously argues the flag is justified as 'unavoidable epistemic cost.' This conflates 'flag sustained' with 'flag is actually correct.' §11.3 is about correctness of the flag, not about whether the compression cost is unavoidable. By accepting the flag as sustained and then reframing the burden as an inherent property of the ritual, the target never adjudicates whether the specific §11.3 flag should be sustained—it grants the flag and shifts to a meta-justification, leaving the audit task itself unperformed.
